title: Python ML: Polynomial Regression
description: If your data points clearly do not fit a linear regression (a straight line), it might be ideal for polynomial regression. Polynomial regression, like linear regression, uses the relationship between the variables x and y to find the best way to draw a line through the data points.
example:
# Polynomial Regression Implementation
import numpy
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = [1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9,10,12,13,14,15,16,18,19,21,22]
y = [100,90,80,60,60,55,60,65,70,70,75,76,78,79,90,99,99,100]

# Create the Polynomial model (4th degree)
mymodel = numpy.poly1d(numpy.polyfit(x, y, 3))

# Visualize the result
myline = numpy.linspace(1, 22, 100)
plt.scatter(x, y)
plt.plot(myline, mymodel(myline))
plt.show()
